data.title: bn-2npu: C018 TCB audit, checker mutation lane, and fair-SCC dead-end kernel fix

data.body:
[HIGH] The new dead-end check rejects a valid EventuallyStateSet certificate after the goal was already reached. reachable_states continues through goal states, scope then includes later non-goal states, and stuck_state returns ProgressDeadlock for initial -> goal -> dead-end. The wire and receipt still identify property code 1 as eventually-state-set at crates/continuum-kernel-temporal/src/verdict.rs:114-157 and property() reports that class at :274-277. The new test at check.rs:1335-1348 confirms that eventuality holds while the checker rejects it as recurrence. continuumd converts this to non-retryable CertificateRejected at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/evidence.rs:1437-1448 and errors.rs:100-121.

Failure modes: valid eventuality evidence is rejected and cannot progress through the daemon; prose silently changes the property into recurrence without a new machine identity. Edge cases: an initial goal followed by a terminal state; a branch that visits a goal before terminating; a post-goal dead end reachable through another goal. Rollback: removing only stuck_state restores the pre-goal false acceptance, so either stop eventuality analysis at goals or add a distinct recurrence property and wire code with an explicit completion policy. Monitoring: count progress-deadlock witnesses whose reachability path visited a goal and alert on property code eventually-state-set. Validation: cover initial->goal->dead-end, initial-goal->dead-end, and initial->dead-end, and assert both kernel verdict and daemon error class.

[HIGH] TCB-01 compares dependency package names, not Cargo package identities. rule_links builds the allowed set from names and accepts any reached name in that set. The imported graph helper collapses package IDs and sources to package names at tools/check_triptych_independence.py:295-309. A dependency alias can therefore resolve an external or alternate-version package named continuum-kernel-core as if it were the trusted workspace crate. The resulting same-name self-edge is also discarded by reach() at :312-325. The gate can report checking-base-links-only-itself while the checker links non-workspace code.

Failure modes: an external same-name package enters the TCB while the covenant stays green, invalidating dependency isolation and the retained C018 evidence. Edge cases: registry versus path sources, multiple versions with one name, renamed dependency keys, and a same-name dependency of the starting crate. Rollback: keep the prior independent boundary checks authoritative and do not publish TCB-01 evidence until this audit preserves package IDs and source/workspace membership. Monitoring: record every reached Cargo package ID and source, and fail on duplicate names or allowed names whose IDs are not workspace-member IDs. Validation: add metadata fixtures with a same-name external package, a second version, and an aliased dependency; each must produce a witness path and fail TCB-01.

[HIGH] TCB-02 is a fail-open lexical signature scan, so it cannot enforce the claimed wire-only public verdict surface. VERDICT_RET recognizes only literal Verdict, Outcome, or CheckedClaim spellings. A public type alias can hide the return type, for example Decision = Verdict with check_decoded(&Certificate) -> Decision. SELF_PARAM also excludes every public self method, including a decoded Certificate method that decides a Verdict, based only on the assumption that methods read an existing decision. Macro-generated and other valid Rust signatures can bypass the regex too. The audit then reports a clean surface while a public non-wire decision path exists.

Failure modes: a checker accepts decoded or engine-owned structures and self-certification returns without TCB-02 failing. Edge cases: type aliases, impl methods on decoded certificates, re-exports, nested function parameter syntax, qualifiers, and macro-generated public APIs. Rollback: retain the existing exact entry-point tests as authority and remove the new TCB-02 claim until the check uses compiler or rustdoc export data. Monitoring: compare an exact exported-function inventory against one approved bytes entry per checking crate and alert on any new exported verdict/claim producer. Validation: add compiling fixtures for an aliased return, a Certificate::check method, a re-exported function, and a macro-generated entry; every fixture must fail TCB-02.

data.reason: Three HIGH blockers: EventuallyStateSet is rejected as recurrence after a goal, TCB-01 collapses Cargo identities to names, and TCB-02 misses valid public Rust verdict entry points.

data.body: [HIGH] TCB-02 remains fail-open after an approved inventory update. public_api records only public aliases at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:392-401. rule_wire_bytes then claims every alias at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:459-465, but performs only one alias pass. I added two public aliases in memory: Decision = HiddenDecision, then HiddenDecision = Verdict. A public decide_decoded(&Certificate) -> Decision plus its generated inventory entries produced findings=[] and left check_certificate as the only reported verdict entry. The new fixtures do not expose this because self_test accepts any finding with the rule tag at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:912-914. Inventory drift alone satisfies that assertion. Failure modes: an in-memory checker route can enter the TCB while C018 reports one wire-only entry. Edge cases: multi-hop aliases in reverse order, private aliases, associated output types, and re-exported aliased functions. Rollback: keep the exact entry tests authoritative and do not publish TCB-02 evidence until alias analysis reaches a fixed point or compiler/rustdoc data replaces it. Monitoring: report unresolved return types and the full alias closure beside every exported producer. Validation: add a compiling two-hop-alias fixture, update its inventory in the fixture, and require the semantic yields-a-verdict diagnostic rather than any rule-tagged failure.

Repair verified at crates/continuum-kernel-temporal/src/check.rs:353-377. Goal states are marked but never expanded. Alternate pre-goal branches remain in scope. Kernel, differential, and daemon cases cover post-goal dead ends, post-goal cycles, initial goals, and branching dead ends.

data.reason: Goal-stopped reachability repairs the false rejection while preserving pre-goal dead-end rejection.

data.body: Repair verified at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:228-283. The rule walks Cargo package IDs, permits only checking-base workspace-member IDs, rejects duplicate names, and reports renamed dependency edges. The companion C023 reader now fails on package identity ambiguity before using its name-keyed graph.

data.reason: The dependency audit now preserves Cargo package identity and fails on names, sources, versions, and aliases.
HIGH: TCB-02 still accepts a decoded-certificate verdict route hidden behind a two-hop alias after the approved inventory is regenerated. See th-lmf9k5.2.

data.body: Repair verified at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:480-510 and :1008-1018. The rule now computes an ordinary alias closure to a fixed point, includes private and associated aliases, and requires each fixture semantic diagnostic. The original two-hop bypass is closed. A distinct generic-default alias bypass is recorded separately.

data.reason: The original ordinary multi-hop alias bypass is repaired at target 81306c780412d5075b6eeaaf72e6117cdada290a; a distinct generic-default bypass has its own thread.

data.body:
[HIGH] TCB-02 still fails open for a valid generic alias with a default type. `ALIAS` at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:463 excludes any `=` inside the generic parameter list. Thus `pub type Decision<T = Verdict> = T;` never joins the closure at :480-510. I overlaid that alias, `pub fn decide(certificate: &crate::wire::Certificate) -> Decision`, and the exact generated inventory entries on the real tree. `rule_wire_bytes` returned `findings=[]`. Rust resolves the omitted type argument to `Verdict`, so this creates a public decoded-input verdict route while the audit stays green.

Failure modes: an in-memory checker route enters the trusted base while C018 reports a wire-only surface. Edge cases: defaulted type parameters, const-generic defaults, associated-type equality in generic bounds, and multi-hop aliases through any such definition. Rollback: keep the exact Rust entry-point tests authoritative and do not publish TCB-02 evidence until alias parsing handles all valid generic syntax or compiler/rustdoc data replaces it. Monitoring: fail on every unresolved alias or return type and record the fully resolved type beside each public producer. Validation: add a compiling fixture with `Decision<T = Verdict>`, its own approved inventory lines, and a required `yields a verdict from non-wire input` diagnostic; also cover a multi-hop and const-generic form.

data.reason: HIGH: TCB-02 omits valid generic aliases with default type parameters, so an approved decoded-input Verdict producer can leave the C018 wire-only audit green. See the open tools/check_tcb_audit.py:463-510 thread.

data.body: Repair verified at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:484-575 and :1076-1086. The rule now rejects generic-default and other non-plain aliases before inventory approval. The four added compiling fixtures require the exact fail-closed diagnostic. Separate public-producer bypasses remain in a new thread.

data.reason: Generic-default alias bypass repaired at a62b097; distinct TCB-02 producer-shape finding tracked separately.

data.body:
[HIGH] TCB-02 still approves valid public non-wire verdict producers. `items` records public consts and statics by name only here, so `rule_wire_bytes` cannot see their function-pointer types. The semantic pass at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:622-648 also ignores a generic return such as `T: From<Verdict> -> T`, and its `SELF.match(params)` exemption accepts extra decoded inputs on a verdict method. I overlaid each case in memory with its exact generated inventory line: a private `fn decide_decoded(&Certificate) -> Verdict` exported as `pub const DECIDE: fn(&Certificate) -> Verdict`, `pub fn decide<T: From<Verdict>>(&Certificate) -> T`, and `impl Verdict { pub fn check_decoded(&self, &Certificate) -> Verdict }`. Each produced `findings=[]`. The Rust entry-point tests only scan literal `pub fn ... -> Verdict`, so they do not close these routes.

Failure modes: decoded or engine-owned structures can enter the trusted base through an approved public producer while C018 reports one wire-only entry. Edge cases: const or static function pointers, generic conversion bounds, methods with additional inputs, and trait-mediated producers. Rollback: keep the exact Rust entry tests authoritative and do not publish TCB-02 as fail-closed until every exported callable value and producer signature is compiler-derived or conservatively refused. Monitoring: record full types for consts and statics, full parameter lists for allowed verdict methods, and unresolved generic return bounds. Validation: add compiling fixtures for all three overlays, approve their inventory lines, and require a semantic non-wire-producer diagnostic.

[HIGH] TCB-05 can accept evidence from a campaign that failed. `--evidence` writes `c018.json` here before it evaluates `failures` and `mismatches` for the exit code. The normal gate then checks only the checker digest and per-id outcomes at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:713-737. It ignores `lane.control`, fixture compilation, summaries, measurements, details, and duplicate evidence rows. A failed generation can therefore overwrite the good record, return 1 once, and let the next `just covenant` pass. The digest at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:196-209 also omits `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and `rust-toolchain.toml`, although the lane copies and uses them at :808-826. The claims matrix trusts these unchecked results at notes/plan/docs/18_CLAIMS_MATRIX.md:181-238.

Failure modes: failed controls or fixture compilation overwrite valid evidence; stale or fabricated measurements remain green; build-input drift retains current status. Edge cases: outcomes match despite a control failure, duplicate ids collapse in the validation dictionary, or one fixture fails compilation after all mutant outcomes were recorded. Rollback: restore the last good record and write a replacement atomically only after every control, fixture, outcome, and invariant passes. Monitoring: reject non-passing controls, false fixture compilation entries, duplicate rows, noncanonical summaries, and omitted build-input identities. Validation: corrupt each retained field, change each copied build input, and simulate a failed generation while asserting normal mode fails and the prior record remains unchanged.

[HIGH] Additional reproduction for this producer-shape class: `FN_SIG` at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:464 accepts only `\w+` function names, and the pass silently continues on a mismatch at :624-627. A valid `pub fn r#try(decoded: &crate::wire::Certificate) -> crate::verdict::Verdict` with its exact approved inventory line also produced `findings=[]`. The literal Rust authority test misses both the raw identifier and qualified return spelling.

[HIGH] The TCB inventory and evidence digest omit compiler inputs outside `src/**/*.rs`. `source_digest` selects only that glob at tools/check_tcb_audit.py:198-209, and `shipped_sources` repeats it here. I overlaid `#[path = "hidden.inc"] mod hidden; pub use hidden::decide;` in `continuum-certificate/src/lib.rs` and a valid `hidden.inc` function that accepts `Family` and returns `Outcome`, then approved the generated `use hidden::decide` inventory line. `rule_wire_bytes` returned `findings=[]`; `hidden.inc` was absent from both `shipped_sources` and the digest. The certificate crate is outside the kernel covenant rule that rejects `#[path]`, and its authority test uses a fixed four-file list at crates/continuum-certificate/tests/inv004_no_self_certification.rs:73-87 and :188-208.

Failure modes: shipped trusted-base code exposes a decoded-input producer while remaining outside TCB-02 inventory and TCB-05 freshness, so later hidden-file changes also keep the retained record current. Edge cases: non-`.rs` modules, paths outside `src`, nested path attributes, and private modules with public re-exports. Rollback: reject path redirection in `continuum-certificate` until the audit derives all compiler inputs from compiler metadata. Monitoring: record every compiler input path and require exact equality with inventoried and digested sources. Validation: add a compiling path-module fixture with an approved re-export line, require a TCB-02 finding, then mutate only the hidden file and require TCB-05 to fail.

data.reason: Three unresolved HIGH findings: TCB-02 approves public non-wire verdict producers (th-ageah1); compiler inputs outside src/**/*.rs evade inventory and freshness (th-vtoiw6); TCB-05 can accept a record written by a failed campaign (th-3qj5i8). The temporal, package-identity, and generic-default-alias repairs are verified. The separate risk:critical human-approval gate remains unchanged.
workspace rebased onto trunk after bn-1ln12; persisted base no longer the merge base. Continued as a new review with the same findings history (rounds 1-4 verified).
